sentences.text: The name Gulosaurus translates to 'Helm's wolverine lizard'.
This animal grew to a length of approximately 1.5 meters.
It is classified as an extinct genus of basal grippidian ichthyopterygian.
Gulosaurus belongs to the class Reptilia.
Unlike many later ichthyopterygians, Gulosaurus possessed pentadactyl limbs instead of polyphalangy.
The skull featured cylindrical anterior teeth, differing from those of Grippia.
Gulosaurus was first described by Cuthbertson, Russell, and Anderson in 2013.
The type species of the genus Gulosaurus is Gulosaurus helmi.
Initially, the incomplete fossil was thought to belong to either Grippia longirostris or Parvinatator wapitiensis.
The discovery of the missing half of the fossil, including the skull, in 2013 confirmed Gulosaurus as a distinct new species.
The flipper structure of Gulosaurus was similar to Grippia, except the first metacarpal had a notched peripheral shaft rather than a lunate shape.
Fossils of Gulosaurus have been found in the Early Triassic Vega-Phroso Siltstone Member of the Sulphur Mountain Formation in east-central British Columbia, Canada.
